podcast.body: Released in 1954, this song by Big Joe Turner is cited as one of the template songs for rock and roll during that era, indicating its foundational influence on the developing genre. "We can go back to Big Joe Turner and his 1954 song Shake, Rattle, and Roll, one of the template songs for rock and roll during that era."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: Recorded seventeen years after "Roll and Pete," this song became Joe Turner's most well-known contribution to popular music. Written by Jesse Stone (under the pseudonym Charles Calhoun), it shows a clear musical lineage to "Roll and Pete," with a similarly structured 12-bar blues form, floating lyrics, and a blues shouting vocal style. The main difference is a much more pronounced backbeat, stressed almost to the point of parody, defining it as a rock and roll song. It was covered by Bill Haley and Elvis Presley and performed on shows promoted by Alan Freed. "The main difference here is that the backbeat is now stressed almost at the point of parody, because Shake, Rattlen, Roll is a rock and roll song."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs
